newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends little changed, Nasdaq again sets record. [CORRECTED 23:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Dow ends little changed, Nasdaq again sets record. [CORRECTED 23:00 GMT]

text.p: U.S. blue chips stocks ended little changed on Tuesday, recovering after an early bout of profit-taking that knocked more than 70 points off the Dow Jones Industrial Average.

Technology stocks rallied, led by gains in personal computer makers Compaq Computer Corp and Dell Computer Corp. The Nasdaq Composite closed at a record high for the third (corrects from seventh) session in a row, finishing 11.16 points higher at 1443.11.

The Dow started the day with a steep decline following the release of the May Consumer Price Index, but it erased the losses and reached new highs before settling back in late trading. The blue chip index closed unofficially at 7760.78, down 11.31.
Analysts said May consumer prices, which rose an expected 0.1 percent from the previous month, sparked some profit-taking even though the data did not suggest that inflation was accelerating.

"Wall Street finally got the news and some just made a sale to hold on to their gains," said Jack Baker, senior managing director of trading at Furman Selz. The Dow has closed at record highs in six of the past eight sessions.
Although the Dow closed with a slight loss, analysts said the partial rebound after early weakness showed the market was still strong.

"You still have a lot of people buying on dips, especially fund managers who need to show they were in the hot stocks before they send out their statements" at the end of the second quarter, said Charles Payne, head analyst at Wall Street Strategies.
Volume was high at about 547 million shares unofficially. Traders said volatility could pick up during the week as the "triple witching" expiration of options and futures on Friday nears.

Looking beyond, one analyst said Tuesday's benign consumer price data, on the heels of a tame producer price report, further reduced the chances the Federal Reserve will move to raise interest rates at its July policy meeting.

"The CPI was the last nail in the coffin for the Fed -- the most important data between now and their July meeting. It looks like clear sailing ahead. The Dow could test 8,000 in the next few weeks," Baker said.
Personal computer stocks rose, bolstered by an optimistic outlook for the quarter and Merrill Lynch's bullish comments on industry bellwether Compaq, which added 2-5/8 to 107-3/4.

Dell surged further, up 5-1/2 to a 52-week high of 120-7/8, after it said Monday it was "very pleased" with its performance in the second quarter. Gateway 2000 Inc, Digital Equipment Corp and Hewlett-Packard also rose.
Analysts said the attention surrounding the PC Expo in New York this week also gave tech stocks a higher profile.

Reynolds & Reynolds Co dropped about 22 percent after it said its earnings for the current quarter would fall short of analysts' expectations. The provider of information management services fell 4-1/8 to 15-5/8. It was the most heavily traded stock on the NYSE.

Amgen Inc slid after said it expected slower sales growth for Epogen, which boosts red blood cell counts, and that the obesity drug Leptin showed disappointing results in a trial. The shares fell 3-9/16 to 58-9/16.

Shares in Nautica Enterprises Inc dropped 1-7/16 to 21-1/4 and Tommy Hilfiger Corp lost 3-1/4 to 40-1/8 after Dillon Read & Co lowered its ratings on the clothing companies, citing weak-than-expected retail trends.
Shares of Portugal's national electric company, Electricidade de Portugal, shot up 8-21/32, or more than 33 percent, to 34-1/2 in its first day of U.S. trading.
The S&P 500 index rose 0.53 to close officially at 894.43, a record. The Nasdaq Composite rose 11.16 points to 1443.11, a record.
